<div id="A3.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">PathFM returns an ensemble in 51.6 ms for one history and 215.2 ms for sixteen.
Batching sixteen histories reduces the average time per history to 13.5 ms.
At both batch sizes, PathFM with one evaluation is faster than Sundial and TimesFM-3.
Chronos-2 and TiRex-2 offer lower latency, while PathFM achieves higher FPS skill (<a href="#S5.F4" title="In 5.3 Accuracy, model size, and inference cost ‣ 5 Forecasting accuracy and efficiency ‣ PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting ofMultivariate Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<section id="A3.SS3.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">C.3.1 </span>Inference speedup breakdown</h4>

<div id="A3.SS3.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS3.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#A3.F12" title="In C.3.1 Inference speedup breakdown ‣ C.3 Inference latency ‣ Appendix C Sampling and computational efficiency ‣ PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting ofMultivariate Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a> isolates execution choices in a separate study on A100.
Packing paths reduces teacher latency from 2,663.8 to 827.1 ms per batch; the packed two-evaluation student takes 201.9 ms.
Adding deeper history K/V caching changes teacher latency only to 801.4 ms and is disabled for the student.
The combined student speedup therefore comes from packing and distillation.
Packing also reduces peak PyTorch allocated memory from 3.22 to 1.58 GiB.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A3.F12" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.22358v1/efficiency_execution.svg" id="A3.F12.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:329/219;" width="329" height="219"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 12: </span>Inference speedup breakdown on an A100 at batch 16, context 2,048, and horizon 480.
The teacher uses ten Euler evaluations; the student uses two.
All configurations use float32 weights with bfloat16 autocast.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Evaluation metrics</h2>

<div id="A4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We specify the empirical forecast scores and aggregation rules used in the forecasting results.
The chaotic-system protocols and diagnostics are given separately in <a href="#A6" title="Appendix F Chaotic systems ‣ PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting ofMultivariate Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<section id="A4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.1 </span>Score construction</h3>

<section id="A4.SS1.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">D.1.1 </span>Empirical forecast scores</h4>

<div id="A4.SS1.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For a fixed outcome <math id="A4.SS1.SSS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> and predictive law <math id="A4.SS1.SSS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>P</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math>, CRPS and energy score have the common form</p>
<table id="A4.E11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{\rho}(P,y)=\mathbb{E}\rho(X,y)-\tfrac{1}{2}\mathbb{E}\rho(X,X^{\prime}),\qquad X,X^{\prime}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{iid}}}{{\sim}}P," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>ρ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>P</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ρ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="false"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝔼</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ρ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>X</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><msup><mi>X</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mover><mo>∼</mo><mi>iid</mi></mover><mi>P</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{\rho}(P,y)=\mathbb{E}\rho(X,y)-\tfrac{1}{2}\mathbb{E}\rho(X,X^{\prime}),\qquad X,X^{\prime}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{iid}}}{{\sim}}P,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(11)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">using absolute and Euclidean distance, respectively <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gneiting &amp; Raftery, 2007</a>)</cite>.
We evaluate the returned empirical forecast <math id="A4.SS1.SSS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widehat{P}_{m}=\frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^{m}\delta_{x^{(i)}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>P</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>m</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>m</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>m</mi></msubsup><msub><mi>δ</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widehat{P}_{m}=\frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^{m}\delta_{x^{(i)}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Substituting this distribution gives</p>
<table id="A4.E12" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{\rho}(\widehat{P}_{m},y)=\frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^{m}\rho(x^{(i)},y)-\frac{1}{2m^{2}}\sum_{i,j=1}^{m}\rho(x^{(i)},x^{(j)})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>ρ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>P</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>m</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>m</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>m</mi></munderover><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>m</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>m</mi></munderover><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{\rho}(\widehat{P}_{m},y)=\frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^{m}\rho(x^{(i)},y)-\frac{1}{2m^{2}}\sum_{i,j=1}^{m}\rho(x^{(i)},x^{(j)}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(12)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">This is the exact score of the finite forecast distribution and requires no independence assumption on its members.
We use <a href="#A4.E12" title="In D.1.1 Empirical forecast scores ‣ D.1 Score construction ‣ Appendix D Evaluation metrics ‣ PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting ofMultivariate Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Equation</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a> for every CRPS and energy component.
The variogram component evaluates the moments of the same empirical forecast (<a href="#A4.E14" title="In Variogram. ‣ D.1.2 Temporal path scores ‣ D.1 Score construction ‣ Appendix D Evaluation metrics ‣ PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting ofMultivariate Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Equation</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">14</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS1.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">D.1.2 </span>Temporal path scores</h4>

<div id="A4.SS1.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For item <math id="A4.SS1.SSS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> and channel <math id="A4.SS1.SSS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math>, define the seasonal-error scale from history <math id="A4.SS1.SSS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> and seasonal period <math id="A4.SS1.SSS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>

<p id="A4.SS1.SSS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Except for first passage, the temporal scores use paths divided by finite positive <math id="A4.SS1.SSS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{nc}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{nc}</annotation></semantics></math>.

</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
<div id="A4.SS1.SSS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Level, sum, and maximum scores use the same observed-coordinate mask for every forecast path.
DES retains the initial value when observed and increments only when both adjacent observations are available.</p>
</div>
<section id="A4.SS1.SSS2.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Variogram.</h5>

<div id="A4.SS1.SSS2.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS2.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For the nonempty set of observed time pairs <math id="A4.SS1.SSS2.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathcal{P}=\{(s,t):s&lt;t,\ y_{s},y_{t}\text{ observed}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo rspace="0.278em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>t</mi><mo rspace="0.667em">,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mtext> observed</mtext><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{P}=\{(s,t):s&lt;t,\ y_{s},y_{t}\text{ observed}\}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="A4.E14" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widehat{\mathrm{VS}}_{1/2}=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{P}|}\sum_{(s,t)\in\mathcal{P}}\left(|y_{s}-y_{t}|^{1/2}-\frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^{m}|x_{s}^{(i)}-x_{t}^{(i)}|^{1/2}\right)^{2}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>VS</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi></mrow></munder><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>m</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>m</mi></munderover><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>x</mi><mi>s</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widehat{\mathrm{VS}}_{1/2}=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{P}|}\sum_{(s,t)\in\mathcal{P}}\left(|y_{s}-y_{t}|^{1/2}-\frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^{m}|x_{s}^{(i)}-x_{t}^{(i)}|^{1/2}\right)^{2}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(14)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS2.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">All pairs receive equal weight <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">Scheuerer &amp; Hamill, 2015</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS1.SSS2.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">First passage.</h5>

<div id="A4.SS1.SSS2.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS2.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The threshold <math id="A4.SS1.SSS2.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> is the maximum of the last available context segment of length at most <math id="A4.SS1.SSS2.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math>, in original units.
For a path <math id="A4.SS1.SSS2.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>u</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>
<table id="A4.E15" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{\tau}(u)=\min\bigl(\{t\in\{1,\ldots,L\}:u_{t}&gt;\tau\}\cup\{L+1\}\bigr)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>τ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>min</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>L</mi><mo rspace="0.278em" stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo>∪</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{\tau}(u)=\min\bigl(\{t\in\{1,\ldots,L\}:u_{t}&gt;\tau\}\cup\{L+1\}\bigr).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(15)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS2.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">This score requires a fully observed future and finite threshold, uses forecast steps as units, and treats no crossing as <math id="A4.SS1.SSS2.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L+1</annotation></semantics></math>.
It therefore evaluates a censored event time.
The sum, maximum, and first-passage scores identify their respective functional distributions rather than the full path law.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS1.SSS3" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">D.1.3 </span>Cross-variable variogram score</h4>

<div id="A4.SS1.SSS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The cross-variable variogram compares channel pairs at the same forecast time.
Channels are standardized by their mean and standard deviation over at most 8,192 context observations; insufficient history or negligible variance excludes a channel.
Using shared observed-coordinate masks, the estimator in <a href="#A4.E14" title="In Variogram. ‣ D.1.2 Temporal path scores ‣ D.1 Score construction ‣ Appendix D Evaluation metrics ‣ PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting ofMultivariate Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Equation</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">14</span></a> averages over valid times and channel pairs, items, origins, and finally tasks with an arithmetic mean.
We report this absolute score.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.2 </span>Aggregation rules</h3>

<section id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Marginal benchmarks.</h5>

<div id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We retain the official within-task reductions for FEV, GIFT-Eval, and TIME <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shchur et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Aksu et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">Qiao et al., 2026</a>)</cite>.
FEV uses nine quantiles at <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{0.1,0.2,\ldots,0.9\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0.1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>0.9</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{0.1,0.2,\ldots,0.9\}</annotation></semantics></math>.
SQL scales errors by <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{nc}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{nc}</annotation></semantics></math> before averaging.
GIFT-Eval and TIME report equally weighted geometric means of task or configuration losses relative to Seasonal Naive.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">fps-bench.</h5>

<div id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">FPS compares each model with Seasonal Naive across six path metrics on the same 94 tasks with valid scores for every model and metric.
For each metric, we average valid items within each channel, then channels and forecast origins, to obtain one loss per task.
Let <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{d,k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{d,k}</annotation></semantics></math> be the model’s loss divided by Seasonal Naive’s loss for task <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math> and metric <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>, clipped to <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0.01,100]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0.01,100</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0.01,100]</annotation></semantics></math>.
The aggregate score is</p>
<table id="A4.E16" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E16.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{FPS}=1-\operatorname{GM}_{d,k}(r_{d,k})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>FPS</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>GM</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{FPS}=1-\operatorname{GM}_{d,k}(r_{d,k}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(16)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{GM}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>GM</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{GM}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the geometric mean with equal weight for each task and metric.
A score of zero matches Seasonal Naive; higher is better.
Individual component skills use the same rule for one metric at a time.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A5" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix E </span>Forecast accuracy and dependence</h2>

<div id="A5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">These experiments examine which aspects of a forecast improve when the model generates complete paths.
We report temporal component scores, evaluate cross-variable relationships, and test explicit dependence completions of quantile forecasts.
Metric definitions and aggregation rules are collected in <a href="#A4" title="Appendix D Evaluation metrics ‣ PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting ofMultivariate Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<section id="A5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.1 </span>Temporal forecast accuracy</h3>

<div id="A5.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#A5.F13" title="In E.1 Temporal forecast accuracy ‣ Appendix E Forecast accuracy and dependence ‣ PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting ofMultivariate Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a> compares the six FPS components for PathFM and the three strongest baselines (selecting the best-performing completion for each).
<a href="#A5.T8" title="In E.1 Temporal forecast accuracy ‣ Appendix E Forecast accuracy and dependence ‣ PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting ofMultivariate Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> reports the full comparison.
For quantile models, independent completion usually gives better temporal scores than comonotone completion, but the latter can improve sum skill.
PathFM achieves the highest skill scores on all six components, with a 10.6% average improvement against the strongest baseline, TimesFM-3.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A5.F13" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.22358v1/fps_component_bars.svg" id="A5.F13.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:548/185;" width="548" height="185"></object>

<section id="A5.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.2 </span>Cross-variable variogram scores</h3>

<div id="A5.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#A5.T9" title="In Task-specific adaptation. ‣ E.2 Cross-variable variogram scores ‣ Appendix E Forecast accuracy and dependence ‣ PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting ofMultivariate Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> compares absolute cross-variable variogram scores on all 35 multi-target fev-bench tasks, retaining all 625 forecast origins.
The score compares pairs of target variables at the same forecast time, using the standardization and reduction in <a href="#A4.SS1.SSS3" title="D.1.3 Cross-variable variogram score ‣ D.1 Score construction ‣ Appendix D Evaluation metrics ‣ PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting ofMultivariate Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D.1.3</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The Gaussian copula uses shrinkage estimates of normal-score residual-rank correlation and a shared AR(1) temporal factor, fitted on four forecast windows ending before the first test origin.
Six short-history tasks use shorter calibration horizons.
The nine marginal quantiles are interpolated linearly, with constant tails outside probabilities 0.1–0.9.</p>
</div>
<section id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Task-specific adaptation.</h5>

<div id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The fitted Gaussian copula estimates dependence parameters from historical forecast–outcome pairs on each benchmark task.
The forecasting weights remain frozen, but the copula introduces task-specific parameter fitting.
We report these adapted references in a separate table group from PathFM and the fixed independent and comonotone completions, which require no additional task-specific parameter fitting at evaluation time.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A5.T9" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 9: </span>Contemporaneous cross-variable variogram scores on 35 multi-target tasks.
Entries are arithmetic task means; lower is better, with the lowest value in each protocol group bold.
Fitted Gaussian references use task-specific calibration.</figcaption>

<td id="A5.T9.2.11.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:10.0pt;padding-right:10.0pt;">0.1469</td></tr>
<tr id="A5.T9.2.12" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A5.T9.2.12.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left" style="padding-left:10.0pt;padding-right:10.0pt;">TimesFM-3</td>
<td id="A5.T9.2.12.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left" style="padding-left:10.0pt;padding-right:10.0pt;">Fitted Gaussian</td>
<td id="A5.T9.2.12.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right" style="padding-left:10.0pt;padding-right:10.0pt;"><span id="A5.T9.2.12.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">0.1420</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A5.T9.2.13" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A5.T9.2.13.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:10.0pt;padding-right:10.0pt;">Toto-2.0-2.5B</td>
<td id="A5.T9.2.13.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:10.0pt;padding-right:10.0pt;">Fitted Gaussian</td>
<td id="A5.T9.2.13.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:10.0pt;padding-right:10.0pt;">0.1533</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.3 </span>Fitted Gaussian temporal copulas</h3>

<div id="A5.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We test whether fitting a Gaussian temporal copula to historical forecast errors improves the path forecasts of frozen quantile models.
Building on the independent and comonotonic completions in <a href="#A5.SS1" title="E.1 Temporal forecast accuracy ‣ Appendix E Forecast accuracy and dependence ‣ PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting ofMultivariate Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E.1</span></a>, we estimate temporal dependence from target-task history while retaining each baseline’s marginal quantile forecasts.</p>
</div>
<section id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Gaussian copula fitting.</h5>

<div id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each baseline and item, four forecast windows ending before the first test origin supply standardized residuals, which we rank-transform to normal scores.
We estimate a lag-one coefficient within these windows, share it across target channels, clip it to <math id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[-0.95,0.95]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.95</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>0.95</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[-0.95,0.95]</annotation></semantics></math>, and fix it before testing.
Items with insufficient information use a task-pooled estimate.
All eligible items are retained; 27 tasks use shorter calibration horizons without changing their test windows.
The fitted coefficient defines a stationary latent AR(1) process used to generate temporally dependent ranks for the baseline’s interpolated marginal quantiles, with constant tails outside probabilities 0.1–0.9.
This parameterization restricts the fitted temporal dependence to AR(1).</p>
</div>
<figure id="A5.T10" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 10: </span>Effect of fitting a Gaussian temporal copula on FPS over 94 common fev-bench tasks.

Fitted Gaussian rows use task-specific calibration.
Bold marks the best value within each protocol group.</figcaption>

<div id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Fitting the Gaussian copula improves FPS from 0.4699 to 0.5077 for Chronos-2, from 0.4871 to 0.5243 for TimesFM-3, and from 0.4261 to 0.4765 for Toto-2.0-2.5B, relative to independent completion.
However, these completions impose a stationary Gaussian AR(1) dependence structure, and PathFM has a higher FPS score without task-specific copula fitting.</p>

</section>
</section>
<section id="A6" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix F </span>Chaotic systems</h2>

<div id="A6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We examine how model size, sampling, and fine-tuning affect point accuracy and long-run dynamics.</p>
</div>
<section id="A6.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.1 </span>Setup and forecasting protocols</h3>

<section id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Dataset.</h5>

<div id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We train PathFM on the PANDA-72M reproduction corpus <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lai et al., 2026</a>)</cite>, <span id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">GilpinLab/dataset-panda72M-repro</span>, containing 190,006 trajectories of 4,096 steps with 3–10 state coordinates from individual DYSTS systems and skew-product combinations.
Reserving trajectories involving ten parent systems leaves 156,784 training trajectories and 33,222 validation trajectories.
Point evaluation uses the separate <span id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">base40</span> and <span id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">skew40</span> test releases.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Models and training.</h5>

<div id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The quantitative comparisons use the 75M and 126M PathFM families with native 256-step horizons, trained for 2M flow-matching updates followed by 100k terminal-decay updates.
We train the 75M variant to approximately match PANDA’s parameter count (74.2M versus 71.6M).
The 126M backbone has 12 transformer blocks and feedforward width 3,072; the 75M model uses 11 blocks and width 768.
Both initialize their backbones afresh while retaining trainable input-patch embeddings.
The global batch budget is 384 channel rows, with four flow draws per window.
The learning rate is <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math> after 500 warmup updates, followed by the 100k linear terminal decay to zero; weight decay is zero and EMA decay is 0.999.
Main results use ten-step Euler sampling, source standard deviation 0.86, and seed 42.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Training-progress evaluation.</h5>

<div id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#S5.F6" title="In Scaling to 300M parameters. ‣ 5.3 Accuracy, model size, and inference cost ‣ 5 Forecasting accuracy and efficiency ‣ PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting ofMultivariate Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>c uses the same 2,048 fixed three-channel validation windows for both model sizes, selected randomly from the validation shard.
Each window supplies 512 context steps and 256 forecast steps from a distinct held-out trajectory.
We evaluate EMA weights with 16 stratified samples and ten Euler steps.
Context-standardized sMAPE is averaged over channels and forecast steps, then across the 2,048 trajectories.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Point forecasts.</h5>

<div id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate six 512-context windows from each of 9,347 trajectories using sMAPE, as in PANDA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lai et al., 2026</a>)</cite>.
We average sMAPE within each of the 480 source groups and then report the arithmetic mean across groups.
PathFM feeds back the coordinatewise median of 16 stratified samples per 256-step block, averaging the middle two order statistics.
Chronos-1 uses 16 samples and median feedback every 128 steps, chaining two native 64-step calls within each sample; Chronos-2 and PANDA continue point forecasts in 128-step blocks.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Long continuations.</h5>

<div id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each of the 135 systems, we generate 4,096-step continuations from origins 512 and 4,096 on an unseen trajectory.
PathFM and Chronos-1 independently continue 16 iid paths per origin; Chronos-2 and PANDA continue point forecasts.
For each diagnostic, we take the arithmetic mean over all realizations in a system.
Across the 135 systems, we use a geometric mean for segment analog and arithmetic means for the other diagnostics.
Segment-analog ratios differ by orders of magnitude across systems because their calibration distances can have very different scales; geometric aggregation gives each system equal weight on a log scale.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.2 </span>Model size and sampler choice</h3>

<div id="A6.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#A6.T11" title="In F.2 Model size and sampler choice ‣ Appendix F Chaotic systems ‣ PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting ofMultivariate Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a> compares PathFM with 72M-parameter PANDA.
The smaller PathFM retains lower errors at all four forecasting horizons and on all four dynamical diagnostics, showing that the gains persist at similar model size.
We obtain these gains with our general forecasting architecture and flow-matching objective, without adding architectural components or losses tailored to chaotic systems.
PANDA uses specialized dynamics embeddings with random polynomial and Fourier features motivated by Koopman-operator approximations <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lai et al., 2026</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A6.T11" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 11: </span>Model size at ten Euler evaluations per block.

<figure id="A6.F14" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.22358v1/chaos_sampler_choices.svg" id="A6.F14.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:548/229;" width="548" height="229"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 14: </span>Accuracy versus sampler budget for both model sizes.
Point errors average all 480 source groups; <math id="A6.F14.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>W</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> averages all 135 systems and uses 4,096-step sampled continuations.
The dotted horizontal line marks PANDA; lower is better.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A6.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The sampler comparison evaluates each teacher and its student after 100k PDD updates (<a href="#A6.F14" title="In F.2 Model size and sampler choice ‣ Appendix F Chaotic systems ‣ PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting ofMultivariate Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figures</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">14</span></a> and <a href="#A6.T12" title="Table 12 ‣ F.2 Model size and sampler choice ‣ Appendix F Chaotic systems ‣ PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting ofMultivariate Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a>).
At one or two evaluations, PDD improves point accuracy over Euler; ten-step Euler remains best within each size at every horizon.
For 126M long continuations, two-evaluation PDD reduces mean <math id="A6.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>W</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> from 0.522 to 0.316 relative to two-step Euler, approaching ten-step Euler’s 0.251.</p>
</div>

NFE counts evaluations per 256-step block and sample; bold marks the lowest error within each size.</figcaption>

<section id="A6.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.3 </span>Full continuations</h3>

<div id="A6.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#A6.F15" title="In F.3 Full continuations ‣ Appendix F Chaotic systems ‣ PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting ofMultivariate Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">15</span></a> extends the qualitative comparison in <a href="#S6.F7" title="In 6.2 What sampling preserves ‣ 6 Forecasting chaotic dynamics ‣ PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting ofMultivariate Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> to all 4,096 steps and adds Rössler.
The displayed PathFM-126M paths use the same checkpoint and ten Euler evaluations per block as the quantitative comparison.
PathFM sustains Lorenz’s two-lobe motion and Rössler’s varying oscillation amplitudes throughout the continuation.
In comparison, Chronos-2 and PANDA both collapse to the center of the Lorenz example.
In the Rössler example, Chronos-2’s amplitude decays and PANDA settles into more regular oscillations.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A6.F15" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2610.22358v1/chaos_full_traces.png" id="A6.F15.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:548/632;" width="548" height="632" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 15: </span>Full 4,096-step Lorenz and Rössler continuations.
All panels use the same initial conditions.
Gray curves show the observed continuation; circles mark the first and last forecast states, and shading marks the first 512 steps.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.4 </span>Metric definitions</h3>

<section id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Point error.</h5>

<div id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">With context channel mean <math id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu_{c}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu_{c}</annotation></semantics></math> and population standard deviation <math id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{c}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{c}</annotation></semantics></math>, let <math id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{x}_{tc}=(x_{tc}-\mu_{c})/\max(\sigma_{c},10^{-10})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>c</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mi>max</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{x}_{tc}=(x_{tc}-\mu_{c})/\max(\sigma_{c},10^{-10})</annotation></semantics></math> and define <math id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{y}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{y}</annotation></semantics></math> identically.
We use PANDA’s factor-100 convention <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lai et al., 2026</a>)</cite>:</p>
</div>

</table>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">This scores the blockwise median forecast; individual sampled-path errors are not averaged into the point score.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Wasserstein-1 distance (<math id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>W</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>).</h5>

<div id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{R}</annotation></semantics></math> be the reference state cloud and <math id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}</annotation></semantics></math> the post-burn-in rollout states, standardized using reference channel means and standard deviations.
For <math id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=64</annotation></semantics></math> seeded unit directions, <math id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widehat{F}_{\mathcal{R},k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>F</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widehat{F}_{\mathcal{R},k}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widehat{F}_{\mathcal{S},k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>F</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widehat{F}_{\mathcal{S},k}</annotation></semantics></math> are the empirical CDFs of the projected states:</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<table id="A6.E18" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.E18.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widehat{W}_{1}(\mathcal{R},\mathcal{S})=\frac{1}{K}\sum_{k=1}^{K}\int_{0}^{1}\left|\widehat{F}_{\mathcal{R},k}^{-1}(u)-\widehat{F}_{\mathcal{S},k}^{-1}(u)\right|\,du." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>W</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>K</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>K</mi></munderover><mrow><msubsup><mo rspace="0em">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>F</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>F</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>u</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widehat{W}_{1}(\mathcal{R},\mathcal{S})=\frac{1}{K}\sum_{k=1}^{K}\int_{0}^{1}\left|\widehat{F}_{\mathcal{R},k}^{-1}(u)-\widehat{F}_{\mathcal{S},k}^{-1}(u)\right|\,du.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(18)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The reference cloud retains at most 20,000 states; this calculation subsamples each cloud to at most 10,000.
It measures distance to an empirical state distribution, without an exact invariant measure.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Spectral distance.</h5>

<div id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Spectral and segment diagnostics standardize channels using trajectories 0–7.
Welch spectra use 512-point periodic Hann windows, 50% overlap, unit sampling rate, and constant detrending.
Each spectrum is normalized to unit mass; <math id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{x,c}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{x,c}</annotation></semantics></math> is the forecast spectrum and <math id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{c}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{c}</annotation></semantics></math> averages the six normalized reference spectra.
The channel-mean squared Hellinger distance is</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<table id="A6.E19" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.E19.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H^{2}_{\mathrm{spec}}=\frac{1}{2C}\sum_{c=1}^{C}\sum_{f}\bigl[\sqrt{p_{x,c}(f)}-\sqrt{q_{c}(f)}\bigr]^{2}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>spec</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>C</mi></munderover><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∑</mo><mi>f</mi></munder><msup><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">[</mo><mrow><msqrt><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msqrt><mo>−</mo><msqrt><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msqrt></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">]</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H^{2}_{\mathrm{spec}}=\frac{1}{2C}\sum_{c=1}^{C}\sum_{f}\bigl[\sqrt{p_{x,c}(f)}-\sqrt{q_{c}(f)}\bigr]^{2}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(19)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">It lies in <math id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math> and compares spectral shape independently of total power.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Correlation dimension.</h5>

<div id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We estimate <math id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widehat{d}_{\mathrm{corr}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>d</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>corr</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widehat{d}_{\mathrm{corr}}</annotation></semantics></math> from log–log slopes of empirical pair-distance probabilities, excluding pairs within a 30-step Theiler window.
The estimator uses at most 4,096 states and 200,000 positive pair distances, taking the median slope over probability ranges <math id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0.005,0.05]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0.005</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.05</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0.005,0.05]</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0.01,0.10]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0.01</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.10</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0.01,0.10]</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0.02,0.20]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0.02</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.20</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0.02,0.20]</annotation></semantics></math>, with 20 geometrically spaced probabilities per range.
Against the dataset’s stored pooled estimate <math id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widehat{d}_{\mathrm{pool}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>d</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>pool</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widehat{d}_{\mathrm{pool}}</annotation></semantics></math>, we report</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<table id="A6.E20" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.E20.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E_{\mathrm{CD}}=\left|\widehat{d}_{\mathrm{corr}}-\widehat{d}_{\mathrm{pool}}\right|." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>CD</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>d</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>corr</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>d</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>pool</mi></msub></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E_{\mathrm{CD}}=\left|\widehat{d}_{\mathrm{corr}}-\widehat{d}_{\mathrm{pool}}\right|.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(20)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The pooled target uses all ten original trajectories, including the test trajectory, and its own standardization; it is a descriptive geometric reference rather than an independent held-out estimate.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Segment analog.</h5>

<div id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Flatten 64-step multivariate segments into vectors in the shared standardized coordinates, without recentering each segment.
Let <math id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{U}_{x}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒰</mi><mi>x</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{U}_{x}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{U}_{\mathrm{ref}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒰</mi><mi>ref</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{U}_{\mathrm{ref}}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{U}_{\mathrm{cal}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒰</mi><mi>cal</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{U}_{\mathrm{cal}}</annotation></semantics></math> denote generated, reference, and calibration segments, and <math id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d(u,\mathcal{U})=\min_{v\in\mathcal{U}}\|u-v\|_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒰</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>min</mi><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒰</mi></mrow></msub><mo>⁡</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d(u,\mathcal{U})=\min_{v\in\mathcal{U}}\|u-v\|_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The score compares their nearest-reference distances:</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<table id="A6.E21" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.E21.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{\mathrm{seg}}=\frac{\operatorname{median}_{u\in\mathcal{U}_{x}}d(u,\mathcal{U}_{\mathrm{ref}})}{\max\!\left\{\operatorname{median}_{u\in\mathcal{U}_{\mathrm{cal}}}d(u,\mathcal{U}_{\mathrm{ref}}),10^{-12}\right\}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>seg</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>median</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒰</mi><mi>x</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒰</mi><mi>ref</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mrow><mpadded style="width:1.808em;" width="1.808em"><mi>max</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><msub><mi>median</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒰</mi><mi>cal</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒰</mi><mi>ref</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow></msup><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{\mathrm{seg}}=\frac{\operatorname{median}_{u\in\mathcal{U}_{x}}d(u,\mathcal{U}_{\mathrm{ref}})}{\max\!\left\{\operatorname{median}_{u\in\mathcal{U}_{\mathrm{cal}}}d(u,\mathcal{U}_{\mathrm{ref}}),10^{-12}\right\}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(21)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Generated and calibration segments use stride 32; reference segments use stride eight, retaining at most 20,000.
The calibration normalization gives a reference level of one; larger values indicate less similar local dynamics.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
